This dataset has 10,868 rows and 6 columns; each row represents one cause–state–year observation from 1999–2017.

**Heart disease and cancer together account for 63.6% of deaths among the specific causes listed.**

- All-cause deaths totaled **47,728,569**, averaging **2,512,030 per year**; the listed specific causes totaled **36,280,583**, averaging **1,909,504 per year**.
- Shares of specific-cause deaths: heart disease **33.7%**, cancer **29.9%**, stroke **7.5%**, CLRD **7.2%**, unintentional injuries **6.5%**.
- Remaining shares: Alzheimer’s **4.1%**, diabetes **3.9%**, influenza/pneumonia **3.0%**, kidney disease **2.4%**, suicide **1.9%**.
- Heart disease was the largest specific contributor (**12,222,640** deaths); suicide was the smallest (**697,016**).
- All-cause deaths rose from **2,391,399 in 1999** to **2,813,503 in 2017**, a **17.7% increase**.
- The largest single national cause-year value was **2,813,503 in 2017**; the IQR outliers are the aggregate all-cause records rather than individual causes.

The trend chart highlights the long-run increase in aggregate mortality and the persistent dominance of heart disease and cancer.
